items.title: Remove escalation carried on the fixed-price Nomad balance
items.close: Exhibit C read for tariff and change-in-law pass-through; decision minuted
items.ev: Rev 3 applies the ESF template rate to the $12.1M contract balance; the price is fixed until Final Acceptance.

items.title: Risk register: labor-cost and material-cost lines overlap the escalation already in the directs
items.close: Re-word the two lines as labor-shortage and tariff risks and size them on exposure, not on the whole material and labor base
items.ev: 'Salaries increase yearly' ($1,020K) and 'material costs increase' ($1,300K) describe escalation, which Rev 3 already carries at $2.95M; a tariff allowance of 15% on $3.69M of non-battery material is $553K.

items.title: Confirm the four written design-basis items Haugland priced as deducts
items.close: Retaining wall, basin, duct bank and GSU count confirmed in writing; HEG map signed first
items.ev: HEG deduct ceiling $1.47M; GSU count already four in Rev 3, so about $0.8M net (red team report).

items.title: Engineering & supervision overhead basis applied to the vendor turnkey contract
items.close: Ruling on whether the E&S station basis applies to vendor-furnished, vendor-commissioned equipment
items.ev: E&S basis rows $4.79M = 16.1% of Station 360 directs; applied to the $13.0M battery line that is 2.1M.

items.title: Commissioning hours carried from E-23-373 overlap Nomad's commissioning support
items.close: Commissioning split (Nomad vs owner) written into the test plan
items.ev: Field test 709K + LCE 408K carried at 2023 hours; the contract already holds $210K of support and $246K of vendor labor.

items.title: Station 496 relay program: 710 man-hours per relay
items.close: Two recent relay-replacement actuals; confirm the four SEL-735 are protection, not metering; outage windows priced
items.ev: 20 relays: hardware $91K, install 6,400 mh ($1.23M), test 7,800 mh ($1.81M), E&S basis $1.46M; $363K per relay all-in. Loaded effect includes the E&S basis on the hours.

items.title: Interconnection topology: five feeder cabinets, four GSUs, four breakers, four metering sets for 10 MW
items.close: Hosting-capacity study: can two feeders take 5 MW each? If not, the item is zero
items.ev: Breakers $1.50M, metering $245K, disconnects $238K, GSUs $1.44M scale with the number of feeder connections.

items.title: Platform and retaining wall sized after geotech, not before
items.close: Geotech report; MassDEP SW45 post-closure permit conditions; NFPA 855 spacing
items.ev: 14-ft retaining wall $470K, earthwork and surfacing $1,040K, 36 borings $361K on a placeholder 2.5-ft platform. Two-sided: the red team's downside is $0.6M to $3.5M.

items.title: Battery installation labor from a crew build-up instead of 25% of a 2023 total; fire suppression bought twice?
items.close: Crew build-up: crane set, anchoring, DC and AC terminations per Voyager unit; confirm whether the Voyager enclosure carries its own suppression ($132K carried)
items.ev: 5,557 mh ($1.07M) for 12 units = 463 mh each; build-up at 200 to 250 mh per unit gives 2,400 to 3,000 mh. NREL ATB installation labor and equipment: $19/kWh (2019$, 60 MW), i.e. about $0.4M at 20 MWh before the small-project premium.

items.title: Disconnect switches and PT cutouts priced as separate lines although the Siemens skids carry them
items.close: Strike lines 07.03.02.04, 06.02.09.00 and the PT cutouts once Siemens confirms the skid scope in writing
items.ev: Siemens budgetary of 12 Aug 2026: $300K per skid for breaker, frame, disconnects, PTs, relays and DC battery (so the $332K breaker line is not a price lever); the 8 disconnects ($238K, 1,040 mh) and PT cutouts are carried again as station lines whose own notes say 'located on breaker skid'.

items.title: GSU installation hours: 524 man-hours per pad-mount; count to be settled (four carried, twelve mentioned)
items.close: Topology and GSU count in writing; crew build-up for a pad-mount set; 2026 transformer quote with the 29-70 week lead time in the schedule
items.ev: Install $363K for four units (524 mh each) against a normal 100-150 mh pad-mount set. The furnish price ($267K each from a 2023 bidder list plus 3%/yr) is not the lever; the count is the exposure (PM email 9 Sep 2026: 'GSU transformers (12)').

items.title: Switchyard lighting: 12 HPS luminaires and $200 a foot of hookup on an unmanned one-acre pad
items.close: Lighting design to the security need (fence-line LED, motion); hookup length and rate from the layout
items.ev: $313K and 1,272 mh across four lighting lines (07.03.02.99).

items.title: Siting and project management: external siting at $1.05M and a $157K siting line inside Station 496
items.close: Task budget from outside counsel for Article 80 small-project review and the ZBA permit; confirm what the Station 496 siting application is for
items.ev: 04.02.00.00 Sta 360 $1,052K external siting; Sta 496 04.02.00.00 $157K for relay work inside an existing fence.

items.title: Section 48E investment tax credit on the storage property
items.close: Eligible-basis opinion; FEOC cost-ratio test (65% non-PFE for a 2028 construction start); normalization election; DPU treatment
items.ev: 30% of an eligible basis of $28M (battery, install, BOP loaded) to $41M (plus station, site, testing). Not an estimate change: a revenue-requirement reduction.

items.title: Energy-community adder if the closed landfill qualifies as a brownfield
items.close: Phase II ESA or a prior brownfield-program assessment (the Phase I safe harbor stops at 5 MW)
items.ev: Additional 10 percentage points on the same basis.

items.title: AFUDC: pay the battery at delivery, not a year ahead; protect the siting float
items.close: Milestone payment schedule in the Nomad SOV aligned to 2028 delivery; float target on the ZBA chain
items.ev: AFUDC $4.7M. Shifting $9.1M of battery payments twelve months later saves about 7.5% of it; every month of schedule slip costs about $0.4M across AFUDC, escalation, PM and indirects (slide 34).

heg_gap_note: Red team KS1: Haugland Class 3 base $19.2M vs Rev 3 B+D+E $8.3M direct; +$4M to +$8M direct if half the gap is 21334 scope. Tier A and B savings are net of nothing until that closes.
